title: Floating in a Pool

beats.line: Core temperature falls, risking mild hypothermia if you stay too long.
beats.idea: Character floats on back, water pushes up with upward arrows around the body.

beats.line: Fingers and toes turn pruney as water causes skin to wrinkle within minutes.
beats.idea: Close‑up of torso and head with red arrows showing blood moving toward the chest and brain.

beats.line: Your heart rate drops as the mammalian diving reflex slows beats to save oxygen.
beats.idea: Heart icon pulses slower, a calm blue glow surrounds the chest.

beats.line: Immersion forces blood toward your chest and head, raising central pressure.
beats.idea: Zoom on hand and foot, skin surface rippling into pruney texture.

beats.line: Buoyancy lifts you, so your body feels almost weightless in water.
beats.idea: Thermometer drops, character shivers, blue frost overlay around the body.

description: A cute paper‑craft cartoon shows the surprising bodily changes when you simply float in a pool.

facts.claim: Buoyancy lifts you, making you feel weightless in water
Water immersion shifts blood toward the chest and head
facts.source: NIH, Cardiovascular response to water immersion

facts.claim: The mammalian diving reflex slows heart rate during facial immersion
Prolonged water exposure causes skin to wrinkle (pruney fingers)
facts.source: Mayo Clinic, Why does skin wrinkle in water?

facts.claim: Extended exposure to cold water can lower core temperature, leading to hypothermia

end.line: Would you stay floating forever, despite the chill?

topic: What happens if you float in a pool?
